properties.name: liveEdgeOffset
properties.documentation: Live edge offset in seconds. How it is applied depends on the type of the segmented representations in the manifest. For `TIMELINE` representations, new segments are held back for this duration (rounded up to whole segments) before they are added to the SegmentTimeline, and are always added in order. This adds the same amount of latency, but a segment that arrives late by up to this duration does not interrupt the manifest. A segment that arrives later than that stops the SegmentTimeline from updating until it arrives. If it does not arrive at all, a placeholder segment is added in its place once a few newer segments are available. If set to 0, segments are added as soon as they are available, still in order. For `TEMPLATE` representations, the `availabilityStartTime` is set this many seconds later, so players request each segment this much later. Late segments do not change the manifest; a player that requests a segment before it is uploaded gets an error. Segments are also kept in the manifest for this duration on top of the timeshift. We recommend a value of at least 2 segment durations.

properties.name: liveEdgeOffset
properties.documentation: Live edge offset in seconds. New segments are held back for this duration (rounded up to whole segments) before they are added to the HLS playlist, and are always added in order. This adds the same amount of latency, but a segment that arrives late by up to this duration does not interrupt the playlist. A segment that arrives later than that stops the playlist from updating until it arrives. If it does not arrive at all, a placeholder segment is added in its place once a few newer segments are available. If set to 0, segments are added as soon as they are available. A late segment is then skipped and inserted into the playlist later, which can make players skip or repeat content. We recommend a value of at least 2 segment durations.
